question: Modern patterned wrapping paper began as a stopgap when a small American card shop ran out of tissue paper one Christmas and sold fancy envelope linings instead. Which famous greeting card company did that shop become?
source_excerpt: Hallmark sold out of the traditional tissue paper at its Halls store in the heart of Kansas City, Mo.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume patterned wrapping paper always existed or came from a paper mill. It actually began as an improvised fix by a card shop, and players already know the brand's name.
extra.verification_notes: Hallmark's Hall Brothers store in Kansas City sold French envelope liners as gift wrap after running out of tissue in 1917; confirmed by Hallmark and NPR/KCUR (https://www.wamc.org/2017-12-23/the-history-of-gift-wrap).

explanation: The shop sold out of the envelope linings, so it started printing decorative paper just for wrapping presents. It was so successful that most of the world now wraps gifts in it.

question: Which 1990s sitcom made the word 'regifting' famous, in an episode where a dentist passes on a label maker he was given?
source_excerpt: The episode is credited with popularizing the term 'regifting.'

extra.why_interesting: Regifting feels like an old social sin with no single origin. The everyday word for it was spread by one sitcom joke about a label maker, and most adults know the show.
extra.verification_notes: Seinfeld's 'The Label Maker' (S6E12, 1995) features dentist Tim Whatley regifting a label maker and popularized 'regifting' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Label_Maker).

explanation: Elaine catches the dentist Tim Whatley handing her own present on to Jerry and labels him a 'regifter'. The word caught on and is now in major dictionaries.
